fact_check.claim: Ithaca Common Council voted 8-2 in July 2024 to opt in; fourth upstate city after Albany, Kingston, Poughkeepsie; Mayor Cantelmo and ITU co-chair Katie Sims backed it
State Good Cause law effective April 20, 2024; Article 6-A sections 210-218; repeal June 15, 2034; applies outside NYC only where a municipality opts in
Increase above the lower of 10% or 5% plus CPI is presumed unreasonable, rebuttable, not a hard cap; DHCR usually publishes CPI by August 1
Right to renew with listed grounds (own residence, demolition, leaving rental market, nonpayment, violation uncured after 10 days' written notice)
Section 216: tenant refusing reasonable renewal terms can be removed with 30-90 days' written notice; nonpayment of an unreasonable increase is not good cause
Certificate of occupancy on or after Jan 1, 2009 exempts a building for 30 years; The Ithacan (built 2023) cited as exempt until 2053
Only college-run dormitories are exempt as a category; no student or fixed-term student lease exemption; WSKG June 2024 summary wrongly said student housing not covered
fact_check.note: brief §2.6 'Dormitory exemption', 'No student exemption'; brief §9 conflict row 'Student housing excluded'.

One search found Ithaca's local-law text defining small landlord as no more than one unit statewide, and a compilation of DHCR's list showing City of Ithaca 345%. The page already hedges that later lists may differ.
